facts.text: Rangeley is named after Englishman Squire James Rangeley, who inherited a 31,000-acre tract bought from Massachusetts in 1796 by his father.
The Phillips and Rangeley Railroad, a narrow‑gauge line that opened in 1891, later joined the Sandy River and Rangeley Lakes Railroad in 1908.
The Rangeley History Museum, housed in a 1905 bank building on the National Register of Historic Places, is the headquarters of the Rangeley Lakes Region Historical Society.
In 2026, the museum will feature a new exhibition titled "Rangeley Region History Makers" celebrating America’s 250th anniversary and the region’s unique heritage.
Rangeley’s extreme temperatures have ranged from 94°F in September 2002 to –45°F in January 1994, showcasing the town’s dramatic climate swings.
The town’s cool mountain climate and abundant sport fishing made it a resort, drawing visitors from Boston, Hartford, New York City, and Philadelphia in the late 19th century.
